title: Coral and the Wolf
premise: Cyrus Amberdale has spent twelve years as the last keeper of the Amberdale Gate, selling harmless charms in a city where magic is a hanging offense, and telling himself the gate behind his shop will stay shut. But when a prophecy written a century ago names tonight's date, the gate opens on its own, and Cyrus learns the 'king' who outlawed magic died years ago — something else wears his crown, feeding on the city's fear to bring an endless winter. Guided by a disgraced prophecy-scholar named Wren and bound by a family oath he never chose, Cyrus must unbind the true king from the thing that replaced him before midwinter seals the gate forever. He succeeds only by surrendering his own inherited magic into the gate, ending the Amberdale line but freeing the king, breaking the winter, and leaving him alive, ordinary, and finally free of both the crown's shadow and his own.
about_author: R. M. Sandoval is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing sealed collections in northern university libraries. Coral and the Wolf is their second novel, following a well-received debut about lighthouse keepers and the sea's long memory.

chapters.title: The Date That Was Promised
chapters.summary: Cyrus, POV. In his charm shop below the forbidden gate, Cyrus finds a century-old prophecy naming today's date and his own surname. He burns it; it rewrites itself. Emotional beat: dread disguised as routine, the moment a careful life begins to crack.

chapters.title: Twelve Years of Small Charms
chapters.summary: Cyrus, POV, with flashback. We learn how he inherited the keeper's oath at nineteen, how his mother vanished through the gate, and why he sells only charms that do nothing. Emotional beat: grief worn smooth by habit, loyalty to a dead woman's instructions.

chapters.title: A Scholar with Stolen Pages
chapters.summary: Wren, POV. Wren, expelled from the Royal Archive for reading what she shouldn't, traces the prophecy to Cyrus's shop and arrives as snow falls out of season. Emotional beat: wary recognition between two people who each hold half a truth.

chapters.title: What the Gate Wants
chapters.summary: Cyrus, POV. The gate unlocks itself at moonrise; through it Cyrus hears his mother's voice asking to be let in. Wren warns it isn't her. Emotional beat: longing weaponized, the first proof that survival means refusing comfort.

chapters.title: The King's Winter Address
chapters.summary: Wren, POV. From a crowd in Coronation Square they watch King Aldric proclaim eternal winter as mercy against plague. Cyrus recognizes the wrongness: the king's shadow moves independently. Emotional beat: civic fear curdling into private certainty.

chapters.title: Charm-Seller, Arrested
chapters.summary: Cyrus, POV. Wardens raid the shop on an anonymous tip; Cyrus escapes through the cellar into the gate's antechamber, taking only his mother's key-ring. Emotional beat: the price of survival made literal — home burned, name posted, past forfeit.

chapters.title: The Archive Beneath the Snow
chapters.summary: Wren, POV. Hiding in a flooded sub-archive, Wren deciphers the prophecy's middle verses: the crown-thing is a hollow called the Wolf, which ate the real king and now eats the realm. Emotional beat: scholar's triumph shadowed by guilt — her reading started this clock.

chapters.title: An Oath in Amber
chapters.summary: Cyrus, POV. Inside the antechamber, a preserved memory shows the first Amberdale binding the Wolf behind the gate — and choosing a descendant as its lock. Cyrus understands he was never a shopkeeper. Emotional beat: inheritance revealed as burden, not gift.

chapters.title: Loyalty, Tested Twice
chapters.summary: Wren, POV. Wren's old mentor offers her reinstatement if she betrays Cyrus's location. She refuses, burning her credentials. Emotional beat: loyalty chosen over safety, and the loneliness that choice brings.

chapters.title: The Court of Hollow Men
chapters.summary: Cyrus, POV. Disguised as a warden's clerk, Cyrus enters the palace and sees the courtiers: all touched by the Wolf, their eyes frosted, their obedience total. He reaches the throne room door and hears the real king screaming beneath the floor. Emotional beat: horror of a world where surrender looks like peace.

chapters.title: Midnight with the Wolf
chapters.summary: Cyrus, POV. The Wolf speaks to Cyrus directly, offering his mother back — it kept her, it claims, as payment on the family debt. Emotional beat: temptation at its most intimate; truth and lie indistinguishable.

chapters.title: What Wren Buried
chapters.summary: Wren, POV. Wren confesses she found the prophecy three years ago and told the Archive, hoping favor would save her career — and the Wolf learned of the keeper because of her. Emotional beat: shame confessed, trust nearly broken, then deliberately rebuilt.

chapters.title: The Unbinding Rite
chapters.summary: Both POVs alternating. They assemble the rite from prophecy and memory: the Wolf can be pulled off the king only at the gate, only by an Amberdale, only at full dark of midwinter eve. Emotional beat: fragile hope built from fragments, partners fully aligned at last.

chapters.title: Hunted Through the Frost Fair
chapters.summary: Cyrus, POV. The frozen river hosts the regime's Frost Fair; wardens corner them among the stalls. Wren holds the line with stolen archive-magic while Cyrus slips toward the palace cisterns. Emotional beat: loyalty proven in blood and cold, cost mounting.

chapters.title: The King Under the Floor
chapters.summary: Wren, POV. In the cisterns they find Aldric — alive, starved, twelve years imprisoned inside his own body's echo. He begs them not to unbind him, believing he deserves the Wolf. Emotional beat: pity for the enemy, the theme of price made flesh.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Gatehouse
chapters.summary: Cyrus, POV. Wren's former mentor leads wardens to the gate; Wren is captured buying them time. The Wolf, wearing the king's shape, orders the gate opened from the outside — the one thing that would end everything. Emotional beat: despair, and the discovery that the prophecy's final verse requires a willing sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Longest Night Begins
chapters.summary: Wren, POV. Imprisoned in the frost-court, Wren talks her way free using the mentor's own archived secrets, and races to warn Cyrus: the rite doesn't just need his magic — it needs all of it, permanently. Emotional beat: resolve sharpened by love neither will name aloud.

chapters.title: Mother's Voice, Mother's Lie
chapters.summary: Cyrus, POV. At the threshold, the gate shows Cyrus the truth: his mother wasn't taken — she entered willingly to slow the Wolf, and left the key-ring as her answer to the same choice. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into inheritance accepted; the wolf and the coral reconciled.

chapters.title: Unbinding
chapters.summary: Both POVs converging. At full dark, Cyrus begins the rite as the Wolf tears free of Aldric and floods the gatehouse in winter. Wren holds the circle while the real king, freed, adds his broken crown-oath to the working. Emotional beat: climax — terror, sacrifice, and the strange calm of doing the inevitable thing.

chapters.title: The Price Paid
chapters.summary: Cyrus, POV. Cyrus pours every thread of Amberdale magic into the gate; the Wolf, starving, is drawn through and locked beyond a seal that no longer needs a keeper. His mother's voice, finally truly hers, says goodbye. Emotional beat: loss and release braided together; the empty quiet after the storm breaks.

chapters.title: Thaw
chapters.summary: Wren, POV. Spring comes early and hard. King Aldric, aged and honest, repeals the magic laws and asks Wren to rebuild the Archive openly. She declines a title but accepts the work. Emotional beat: cautious renewal, institutions mended by people rather than crowns.

chapters.title: Coral and the Wolf
chapters.summary: Cyrus, POV. Cyrus reopens the shop under a new sign, selling charms that still do nothing — except now he tells customers the truth about that. Wren visits with tea and untranslatable pages. Behind the wall, the gate sleeps, unlocked but unneeded. Emotional beat: peace earned, not granted; an ordinary life chosen at last.
